story.what_it_does: Hero MotoCorp makes and sells motorcycles and scooters, mainly in India, and also sells spare parts, exports, and its VIDA electric scooters. In FY2025-26 it sold 64.69 lakh units and earned record revenue of ₹46,830 crore and profit after tax of ₹5,268 crore.
story.plans: Management plans capex of about ₹1,500 crore in FY27, doubling EV and scooter capacity (VIDA to 45,000 units a month by end FY27), and starting Brazil operations in FY2026-27. It also targets a 14-16% medium-term EBITDA margin and a new Global Parts Centre 2.0.
story.moat: Hero leads entry motorcycles with 58.9% share in FY26 and about 91% share in the Splendor 100cc segment. Its scale, parts and accessories business, and growing exports (402,786 units) add to its position.

scenarios.story: Strong industry demand (July retail up 28%) and growth in scooters, EVs and exports lift volumes, while price increases and richer mix help revenue. If commodity costs ease, margins could return to the 14-16% target.
signals_to_watch: EBITDA margin returning to the 14-16% range
VIDA capacity reaching 45,000 units a month by Q4 FY27

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps growing faster than profit as commodity costs hold the EBITDA margin around 13.3-13.4%. Management expects margins to stay stable in Q3 but gives no date for the 14-16% target.
signals_to_watch: Q3 EBITDA margin versus 13.4% in Q2

scenarios.story: Commodity inflation from the West Asia conflict and rare earth magnet shortages persist and price hikes only partly offset them. Market share slips and export disruptions in Colombia, about 25% of exports, hurt growth.
signals_to_watch: Overall retail market share (VAHAN) trend after the reported drop of about 150 basis points
Export growth and disruption in Colombia and Bangladesh
